discovery: Discovery of topological and geometric phases in quantum mechanics (the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University and Chapman University

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm, 1959) showed that electromagnetic potentials, not just fields, have direct physical consequences: a charged particle acquires a measurable phase on circling a region it never enters. Tonomura's electron-holography experiments confirmed this beyond doubt. Berry (1984) revealed the general principle beneath it: a quantum state transported cyclically around a parameter space acquires a geometric phase set by the space's geometry alone. Together these discoveries changed how physicists understand gauge potentials, nonlocality and the geometry of quantum states. They now underpin the theory of topological insulators and the quantum Hall effect, polarization in solids, anyonic statistics, and geometric quantum gates, and they are routinely measured in photonic, atomic and condensed-matter systems. Both answered questions once considered meaningless, and in doing so reshaped quantum theory and opened entire experimental fields.
